CIG_DATA_TYPE_NV_BLOB.doc: Nvidia specific data blob used for Vulkan and other NV clients.

CUDA_ERROR_ALREADY_ACQUIRED.doc: This indicates that a resource has already been acquired.

CUDA_ERROR_ALREADY_MAPPED.doc: This indicates that the resource is already mapped.

CUDA_ERROR_ARRAY_IS_MAPPED.doc: This indicates that the specified array is currently mapped and thus cannot be destroyed.

CUDA_ERROR_ASSERT.doc:
A device-side assert triggered during kernel execution.

The context cannot be used anymore, and must be destroyed. All existing device memory allocations from this context are invalid and must be reconstructed if the program is to continue using CUDA.

CUDA_ERROR_CALL_REQUIRES_NEWER_DRIVER.doc:
This indicates that the API call requires a newer CUDA driver than the one currently installed.

Users should install an updated NVIDIA CUDA driver to allow the API call to succeed.

CUDA_ERROR_CAPTURED_EVENT.doc: This error indicates that the operation is not permitted on an event which was last recorded in a capturing stream.

CUDA_ERROR_CDP_NOT_SUPPORTED.doc: This error indicates that the module is using CUDA Dynamic Parallelism, but the current configuration, like MPS, does not support it.

CUDA_ERROR_CDP_VERSION_MISMATCH.doc: This error indicates that a module contains an unsupported interaction between different versions of CUDA Dynamic Parallelism.

CUDA_ERROR_COMPAT_NOT_SUPPORTED_ON_DEVIC.doc:
This error indicates that the system was upgraded to run with forward compatibility but the visible hardware detected by CUDA does not support this configuration.

Refer to the compatibility documentation for the supported hardware matrix or ensure that only supported hardware is visible during initialization via the CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES environment variable.

CUDA_ERROR_CONTAINED.doc:
This indicates that an exception occurred on the device that is now contained by the GPU’s error containment capability.

Common causes are - a. Certain types of invalid accesses of peer GPU memory over nvlink b. Certain classes of hardware errors This leaves the process in an inconsistent state and any further CUDA work will return the same error. To continue using CUDA, the process must be terminated and relaunched.

CUDA_ERROR_CONTEXT_ALREADY_CURRENT.doc: This indicated that the context being supplied as a parameter to the API call was already the active context.

CUDA_ERROR_CONTEXT_ALREADY_IN_USE.doc: This indicates that the [CUcontext](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1gaf9f5bd81658f866613785b3a0bb7d7d9) passed to the API call can only be bound to a single CPU thread at a time but is already bound to a CPU thread.

CUDA_ERROR_CONTEXT_IS_DESTROYED.doc: This error indicates that the context current to the calling thread has been destroyed using cuCtxDestroy, or is a primary context which has not yet been initialized.

CUDA_ERROR_COOPERATIVE_LAUNCH_TOO_LARGE.doc: This error indicates that the number of blocks launched per grid for a kernel that was launched via either [cuLaunchCooperativeKernel](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__EXEC.html#group__cuda__exec_1ga06d753134145c4584c0c62525c1894cb) or [cuLaunchCooperativeKernelMultiDevice](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__EXEC__DEPRECATED.html#group__cuda__exec__deprecated_1gac4ae8a24130e1e7938514f7e28c76bad) exceeds the maximum number of blocks as allowed by [cuOccupancyMaxActiveBlocksPerMultiprocessor](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__OCCUPANCY.html#group__cuda__occupancy_1gacc6e1094d05cba2cee17fe33ddd04a98) or [cuOccupancyMaxActiveBlocksPerMultiprocessorWithFlags](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__OCCUPANCY.html#group__cuda__occupancy_1ga8f1da4d4983e5c3025447665423ae2c2) times the number of multiprocessors as specified by the device attribute [CU_DEVICE_ATTRIBUTE_MULTIPROCESSOR_COUNT](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1ggae12b8a782bebe21b1ac0091bf9f4e2a3ab92d0a38a94a3f61d4c53e00114afcaa).

CUDA_ERROR_DEINITIALIZED.doc: This indicates that the CUDA driver is in the process of shutting down.

CUDA_ERROR_DEVICE_NOT_LICENSED.doc: This error indicates that the Grid license is not applied.

CUDA_ERROR_DEVICE_UNAVAILABLE.doc:
This indicates that requested CUDA device is unavailable at the current time.

Devices are often unavailable due to use of [CU_COMPUTEMODE_EXCLUSIVE_PROCESS](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1gga637aab2eadb52e1c1c048b8bad9592d1a548bd978657bfc572652dfaf2650209c) or [CU_COMPUTEMODE_PROHIBITED](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1gga637aab2eadb52e1c1c048b8bad9592d1adb8a226241187db3b1f41999bb70eb47).

CUDA_ERROR_ECC_UNCORRECTABLE.doc: This indicates that an uncorrectable ECC error was detected during execution.

CUDA_ERROR_EXTERNAL_DEVICE.doc:
This indicates that an error has occurred in a device outside of GPU.

It can be a synchronous error with respect to CUDA API or an asynchronous error from the external device. In case of asynchronous error, it means that if CUDA was waiting for an external device’s signal before consuming shared data, the external device signaled an error indicating that the data is not valid for consumption. This leaves the process in an inconsistent state and any further CUDA work will return the same error. To continue using CUDA, the process must be terminated and relaunched. In case of synchronous error, it means that one or more external devices have encountered an error and cannot complete the operation.

CUDA_ERROR_FABRIC_NOT_READY.doc:
The GPU fabric is not ready within the bounded wait while the fabric manager probe is still in progress (or not converging in time).

Applications may retry after a delay; for the initialization wait budget, see environment variables such as CUDA_FABRIC_INIT_TIMEOUT_MS. The CUDA Runtime uses the same value as ::cudaErrorFabricNotReady.

CUDA_ERROR_FILE_NOT_FOUND.doc: This indicates that the file specified was not found.

CUDA_ERROR_FUNCTION_NOT_LOADED.doc: Indiciates a function handle is not loaded when calling an API that requires a loaded function.

CUDA_ERROR_GRAPH_EXEC_UPDATE_FAILURE.doc: This error indicates that the graph update was not performed because it included changes which violated constraints specific to instantiated graph update.

CUDA_ERROR_GRAPH_RECAPTURE_FAILURE.doc: This error indicates that a graph recapture failed and had to be terminated.

CUDA_ERROR_HARDWARE_STACK_ERROR.doc:
While executing a kernel, the device encountered a stack error.

This can be due to stack corruption or exceeding the stack size limit. This leaves the process in an inconsistent state and any further CUDA work will return the same error. To continue using CUDA, the process must be terminated and relaunched.

CUDA_ERROR_HOST_MEMORY_ALREADY_REGISTERE.doc: This error indicates that the memory range passed to cuMemHostRegister() has already been registered.

CUDA_ERROR_HOST_MEMORY_NOT_REGISTERED.doc: This error indicates that the pointer passed to [cuMemHostUnregister()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__MEM.html#group__cuda__mem_1ga63f450c8125359be87b7623b1c0b2a14) does not correspond to any currently registered memory region.

CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS.doc:
While executing a kernel, the device encountered a load or store instruction on an invalid memory address.

This leaves the process in an inconsistent state and any further CUDA work will return the same error. To continue using CUDA, the process must be terminated and relaunched.

CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_INSTRUCTION.doc:
While executing a kernel, the device encountered an illegal instruction.

This leaves the process in an inconsistent state and any further CUDA work will return the same error. To continue using CUDA, the process must be terminated and relaunched.

CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_STATE.doc: This indicates that a resource required by the API call is not in a valid state to perform the requested operation.

CUDA_ERROR_INSUFFICIENT_LOADER_VERSION.doc: This indicates that the Loader version is insufficient for fatbin.

CUDA_ERROR_INVALID_ADDRESS_SPACE.doc:
While executing a kernel, the device encountered an instruction which can only operate on memory locations in certain address spaces (global, shared, or local), but was supplied a memory address not belonging to an allowed address space.

This leaves the process in an inconsistent state and any further CUDA work will return the same error. To continue using CUDA, the process must be terminated and relaunched.

CUDA_ERROR_INVALID_CLUSTER_SIZE.doc: Indicates a kernel launch error due to cluster misconfiguration.

CUDA_ERROR_INVALID_CONTEXT.doc:
This most frequently indicates that there is no context bound to the current thread.

This can also be returned if the context passed to an API call is not a valid handle (such as a context that has had cuCtxDestroy() invoked on it). This can also be returned if a user mixes different API versions (i.e. 3010 context with 3020 API calls). See [cuCtxGetApiVersion()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__CTX.html#group__cuda__ctx_1ga088a90490dafca5893ef6fbebc8de8fb) for more details. This can also be returned if the green context passed to an API call was not converted to a [CUcontext](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1gaf9f5bd81658f866613785b3a0bb7d7d9) using [cuCtxFromGreenCtx](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__GREEN__CONTEXTS.html#group__cuda__green__contexts_1gaf0779ec72ce1d5d7eb003d7d9b25afcb) API.

CUDA_ERROR_INVALID_DEVICE.doc: This indicates that the device ordinal supplied by the user does not correspond to a valid CUDA device or that the action requested is invalid for the specified device.

CUDA_ERROR_INVALID_GRAPHICS_CONTEXT.doc: This indicates an error with OpenGL or DirectX context.

CUDA_ERROR_INVALID_HANDLE.doc:
This indicates that a resource handle passed to the API call was not valid.

Resource handles are opaque types like [CUstream](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1gab946c7f02e09efd788a204718015d88a) and [CUevent](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1ga6d740185cf0953636d4ae37f68d7559b).

CUDA_ERROR_INVALID_IMAGE.doc:
This indicates that the device kernel image is invalid.

This can also indicate an invalid CUDA module.

CUDA_ERROR_INVALID_PC.doc:
While executing a kernel, the device program counter wrapped its address space.

This leaves the process in an inconsistent state and any further CUDA work will return the same error. To continue using CUDA, the process must be terminated and relaunched.

CUDA_ERROR_INVALID_PTX.doc: This indicates that a PTX JIT compilation failed.

CUDA_ERROR_INVALID_RESOURCE_CONFIGURATIO.doc: This error indicates one or more resources are insufficient or non-applicable for the operation.

CUDA_ERROR_INVALID_RESOURCE_TYPE.doc: This error indicates one or more resources passed in are not valid resource types for the operation.

CUDA_ERROR_INVALID_SOURCE.doc:
This indicates that the device kernel source is invalid.

This includes compilation/linker errors encountered in device code or user error.

CUDA_ERROR_INVALID_VALUE.doc: This indicates that one or more of the parameters passed to the API call is not within an acceptable range of values.

CUDA_ERROR_JIT_COMPILATION_DISABLED.doc: This indicates that the PTX JIT compilation was disabled.

CUDA_ERROR_JIT_COMPILER_NOT_FOUND.doc: This indicates that the PTX JIT compiler library was not found.

CUDA_ERROR_KEY_ROTATION.doc: This error indicates that an error happened during the key rotation sequence.

CUDA_ERROR_LAUNCH_FAILED.doc:
An exception occurred on the device while executing a kernel.

Common causes include dereferencing an invalid device pointer and accessing out of bounds shared memory. Less common cases can be system specific - more information about these cases can be found in the system specific user guide. This leaves the process in an inconsistent state and any further CUDA work will return the same error. To continue using CUDA, the process must be terminated and relaunched.

CUDA_ERROR_LAUNCH_INCOMPATIBLE_TEXTURING.doc: This error indicates a kernel launch that uses an incompatible texturing mode.

CUDA_ERROR_LAUNCH_OUT_OF_RESOURCES.doc:
This indicates that a launch did not occur because it did not have appropriate resources.

This error usually indicates that the user has attempted to pass too many arguments to the device kernel, or the kernel launch specifies too many threads for the kernel’s register count. Passing arguments of the wrong size (i.e. a 64-bit pointer when a 32-bit int is expected) is equivalent to passing too many arguments and can also result in this error.

CUDA_ERROR_LAUNCH_TIMEOUT.doc:
This indicates that the device kernel took too long to execute.

This can only occur if timeouts are enabled - see the device attribute [CU_DEVICE_ATTRIBUTE_KERNEL_EXEC_TIMEOUT](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1ggae12b8a782bebe21b1ac0091bf9f4e2a3a019c82d47b139b18af14b30db46aeccf) for more information. This leaves the process in an inconsistent state and any further CUDA work will return the same error. To continue using CUDA, the process must be terminated and relaunched.

CUDA_ERROR_LOSSY_QUERY.doc:
This indicates an attempt was made to introspect an object in a way that would discard semantically important information.

This is either due to the object using funtionality newer than the API version used to introspect it or omission of optional return arguments.

CUDA_ERROR_MAP_FAILED.doc: This indicates that a map or register operation has failed.

CUDA_ERROR_MISALIGNED_ADDRESS.doc:
While executing a kernel, the device encountered a load or store instruction on a memory address which is not aligned.

This leaves the process in an inconsistent state and any further CUDA work will return the same error. To continue using CUDA, the process must be terminated and relaunched.

CUDA_ERROR_MPS_CLIENT_TERMINATED.doc:
This error indicates that the MPS client has been terminated by the server.

To continue using CUDA, the process must be terminated and relaunched.

CUDA_ERROR_MPS_CONNECTION_FAILED.doc: This error indicates that the MPS client failed to connect to the MPS control daemon or the MPS server.

CUDA_ERROR_MPS_MAX_CLIENTS_REACHED.doc: This error indicates that the hardware resources required to create MPS client have been exhausted.

CUDA_ERROR_MPS_MAX_CONNECTIONS_REACHED.doc: This error indicates the hardware resources required to support device connections have been exhausted.

CUDA_ERROR_MPS_RPC_FAILURE.doc: This error indicates that the remote procedural call between the MPS server and the MPS client failed.

CUDA_ERROR_MPS_SERVER_NOT_READY.doc:
This error indicates that the MPS server is not ready to accept new MPS client requests.

This error can be returned when the MPS server is in the process of recovering from a fatal failure.

CUDA_ERROR_MULTICAST_RESOURCE_FULL.doc: The API call failed because of a hardware resource required to bind memory to a multicast object is unavailable.

CUDA_ERROR_NOT_FOUND.doc:
This indicates that a named symbol was not found.

Examples of symbols are global/constant variable names, driver function names, texture names, and surface names.

CUDA_ERROR_NOT_INITIALIZED.doc: This indicates that the CUDA driver has not been initialized with [cuInit()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__INITIALIZE.html#group__cuda__initialize_1ga0a2f1517e1bd8502c7194c3a8c134bc3) or that initialization has failed.

CUDA_ERROR_NOT_MAPPED.doc: This indicates that a resource is not mapped.

CUDA_ERROR_NOT_MAPPED_AS_ARRAY.doc: This indicates that a mapped resource is not available for access as an array.

CUDA_ERROR_NOT_MAPPED_AS_POINTER.doc: This indicates that a mapped resource is not available for access as a pointer.

CUDA_ERROR_NOT_PERMITTED.doc: This error indicates that the attempted operation is not permitted.

CUDA_ERROR_NOT_READY.doc:
This indicates that asynchronous operations issued previously have not completed yet.

This result is not actually an error, but must be indicated differently than [CUDA_SUCCESS](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1ggac6c391505e117393cc2558fff6bfc2e9aa0eed720f8a87cd1c5fd1c453bc7a03d) (which indicates completion). Calls that may return this value include [cuEventQuery()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__EVENT.html#group__cuda__event_1ga6f0704d755066b0ee705749ae911deef) and [cuStreamQuery()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__STREAM.html#group__cuda__stream_1ga1b0d24bbe97fa68e4bc511fb6adfeb0b).

CUDA_ERROR_NOT_SUPPORTED.doc: This error indicates that the attempted operation is not supported on the current system or device.

CUDA_ERROR_NO_BINARY_FOR_GPU.doc:
This indicates that there is no kernel image available that is suitable for the device.

This can occur when a user specifies code generation options for a particular CUDA source file that do not include the corresponding device configuration.

CUDA_ERROR_NO_DEVICE.doc: This indicates that no CUDA-capable devices were detected by the installed CUDA driver.

CUDA_ERROR_NVLINK_UNCORRECTABLE.doc: This indicates that an uncorrectable NVLink error was detected during the execution.

CUDA_ERROR_OPERATING_SYSTEM.doc: This indicates that an OS call failed.

CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY.doc: The API call failed because it was unable to allocate enough memory or other resources to perform the requested operation.

CUDA_ERROR_PEER_ACCESS_ALREADY_ENABLED.doc: This error indicates that a call to [cuCtxEnablePeerAccess()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__PEER__ACCESS.html#group__cuda__peer__access_1ga0889ec6728e61c05ed359551d67b3f5a) is trying to re-enable peer access to a context which has already had peer access to it enabled.

CUDA_ERROR_PEER_ACCESS_NOT_ENABLED.doc: This error indicates that [cuCtxDisablePeerAccess()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__PEER__ACCESS.html#group__cuda__peer__access_1ga5b4b6936ea868d4954ce4d841a3b4810) is trying to disable peer access which has not been enabled yet via [cuCtxEnablePeerAccess()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__PEER__ACCESS.html#group__cuda__peer__access_1ga0889ec6728e61c05ed359551d67b3f5a).

CUDA_ERROR_PEER_ACCESS_UNSUPPORTED.doc: This indicates that peer access is not supported across the given devices.

CUDA_ERROR_PRIMARY_CONTEXT_ACTIVE.doc: This error indicates that the primary context for the specified device has already been initialized.

CUDA_ERROR_PROFILER_DISABLED.doc:
This indicates profiler is not initialized for this run.

This can happen when the application is running with external profiling tools like visual profiler.

CUDA_ERROR_SHARED_OBJECT_INIT_FAILED.doc: This indicates that initialization of a shared object failed.

CUDA_ERROR_SHARED_OBJECT_SYMBOL_NOT_FOUN.doc: This indicates that a link to a shared object failed to resolve.

CUDA_ERROR_STREAM_CAPTURE_IMPLICIT.doc: This error indicates a disallowed implicit dependency on a current capture sequence from cudaStreamLegacy.

CUDA_ERROR_STREAM_CAPTURE_INVALIDATED.doc: This error indicates that the current capture sequence on the stream has been invalidated due to a previous error.

CUDA_ERROR_STREAM_CAPTURE_ISOLATION.doc:
This error indicates that a dependency would have been created which crosses the capture sequence boundary.

Only implicit in-stream ordering dependencies are allowed to cross the boundary.

CUDA_ERROR_STREAM_CAPTURE_MERGE.doc: This error indicates that the operation would have resulted in a merge of two independent capture sequences.

CUDA_ERROR_STREAM_CAPTURE_UNJOINED.doc: This error indicates that the capture sequence contains a fork that was not joined to the primary stream.

CUDA_ERROR_STREAM_CAPTURE_UNMATCHED.doc: This error indicates that the capture was not initiated in this stream.

CUDA_ERROR_STREAM_CAPTURE_UNSUPPORTED.doc: This error indicates that the operation is not permitted when the stream is capturing.

CUDA_ERROR_STREAM_CAPTURE_WRONG_THREAD.doc: A stream capture sequence not initiated with the [`CUstreamCaptureMode::CU_STREAM_CAPTURE_MODE_RELAXED`] argument to cuStreamBeginCapture was passed to [cuStreamEndCapture](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__STREAM.html#group__cuda__stream_1ga03dab8b2ba76b00718955177a929970c) in a different thread.

CUDA_ERROR_STREAM_DETACHED.doc:
This error indicates that the requested operation is not permitted because the stream is in a detached state.

This can occur if the green context associated with the stream has been destroyed, limiting the stream’s operational capabilities.

CUDA_ERROR_STUB_LIBRARY.doc:
This indicates that the CUDA driver that the application has loaded is a stub library.

Applications that run with the stub rather than a real driver loaded will result in CUDA API returning this error.

CUDA_ERROR_SYSTEM_DRIVER_MISMATCH.doc:
This error indicates that there is a mismatch between the versions of the display driver and the CUDA driver.

Refer to the compatibility documentation for supported versions.

CUDA_ERROR_SYSTEM_NOT_READY.doc:
This error indicates that the system is not yet ready to start any CUDA work.

To continue using CUDA, verify the system configuration is in a valid state and all required driver daemons are actively running. More information about this error can be found in the system specific user guide.

CUDA_ERROR_TENSOR_MEMORY_LEAK.doc:
An exception occurred on the device while exiting a kernel using tensor memory: the tensor memory was not completely deallocated.

This leaves the process in an inconsistent state and any further CUDA work will return the same error. To continue using CUDA, the process must be terminated and relaunched.

CUDA_ERROR_TIMEOUT.doc: This error indicates that the timeout specified for the wait operation has lapsed.

CUDA_ERROR_TOO_MANY_PEERS.doc: This error indicates that the hardware resources required to enable peer access have been exhausted for one or more of the devices passed to [cuCtxEnablePeerAccess()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__PEER__ACCESS.html#group__cuda__peer__access_1ga0889ec6728e61c05ed359551d67b3f5a).

CUDA_ERROR_UNKNOWN.doc: This indicates that an unknown internal error has occurred.

CUDA_ERROR_UNMAP_FAILED.doc: This indicates that an unmap or unregister operation has failed.

CUDA_ERROR_UNSUPPORTED_DEVSIDE_SYNC.doc: This indicates that the code to be compiled by the PTX JIT contains unsupported call to cudaDeviceSynchronize.

CUDA_ERROR_UNSUPPORTED_EXEC_AFFINITY.doc: This indicates that the [CUexecAffinityType](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1ga14e6345acf2bda65be91eda77cf03f5c) passed to the API call is not supported by the active device.

CUDA_ERROR_UNSUPPORTED_LIMIT.doc: This indicates that the [CUlimit](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1gae24c2d4214af24139020f1aecaf32665) passed to the API call is not supported by the active device.

CUDA_ERROR_UNSUPPORTED_PTX_VERSION.doc: This indicates that the provided PTX was compiled with an unsupported toolchain.

CUDA_GRAPH_INSTANTIATE_CONDITIONAL_HANDL.doc: One or more conditional handles are not associated with conditional nodes.

CUDA_GRAPH_INSTANTIATE_ERROR.doc: Instantiation failed for an unexpected reason which is described in the return value of the function.

CUDA_GRAPH_INSTANTIATE_FLAG_AUTO_FREE_ON.doc: Automatically free memory allocated in a graph before relaunching.

CUDA_GRAPH_INSTANTIATE_FLAG_DEVICE_LAUNC.doc:
Instantiate the graph to be launchable from the device.

This flag can only be used on platforms which support unified addressing. This flag cannot be used in conjunction with [`CUgraphInstantiate_flags::CUDA_GRAPH_INSTANTIATE_FLAG_AUTO_FREE_ON_LAUNCH`].

CUDA_GRAPH_INSTANTIATE_FLAG_UPLOAD.doc:
Automatically upload the graph after instantiation.

Only supported by [cuGraphInstantiateWithParams](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__GRAPH.html#group__cuda__graph_1ga8d9541e4df43ee8440e794634a0d1af8). The upload will be performed using the stream provided in `instantiateParams`.

CUDA_GRAPH_INSTANTIATE_FLAG_USE_NODE_PRI.doc: Run the graph using the per-node priority attributes rather than the priority of the stream it is launched into.

CUDA_GRAPH_INSTANTIATE_INVALID_STRUCTURE.doc: Instantiation failed due to invalid structure, such as cycles.

CUDA_GRAPH_INSTANTIATE_MULTIPLE_CTXS_NOT.doc: Instantiation for device launch failed due to the nodes belonging to different contexts.

CUDA_GRAPH_INSTANTIATE_NODE_OPERATION_NO.doc: Instantiation for device launch failed because the graph contained an unsupported operation.

CUDA_SUCCESS.doc:
The API call returned with no errors.

In the case of query calls, this also means that the operation being queried is complete (see [cuEventQuery()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__EVENT.html#group__cuda__event_1ga6f0704d755066b0ee705749ae911deef) and [cuStreamQuery()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__STREAM.html#group__cuda__stream_1ga1b0d24bbe97fa68e4bc511fb6adfeb0b)).

CU_ACCESS_PROPERTY_PERSISTING.doc: Persisting access is more likely to persist in cache.

CU_ACCESS_PROPERTY_STREAMING.doc: Streaming access is less likely to persit from cache.

CU_AD_FORMAT_AYUV.doc: 4 channel, 8-bit YUV packed planar format, with 4:4:4 sampling.

CU_AD_FORMAT_BC1_UNORM.doc: 4 channel unsigned normalized block-compressed (BC1 compression) format.

CU_AD_FORMAT_BC1_UNORM_SRGB.doc: 4 channel unsigned normalized block-compressed (BC1 compression) format with sRGB encoding.

CU_AD_FORMAT_BC2_UNORM.doc: 4 channel unsigned normalized block-compressed (BC2 compression) format.

CU_AD_FORMAT_BC2_UNORM_SRGB.doc: 4 channel unsigned normalized block-compressed (BC2 compression) format with sRGB encoding.

CU_AD_FORMAT_BC3_UNORM.doc: 4 channel unsigned normalized block-compressed (BC3 compression) format.

CU_FUNC_ATTRIBUTE_BINARY_VERSION.doc:
The binary architecture version for which the function was compiled.

This value is the major binary version \* 10 + the minor binary version, so a binary version 1.3 function would return the value 13. Note that this will return a value of 10 for legacy cubins that do not have a properly-encoded binary architecture version.

If the user-specified dynamic shared memory size is larger than this value, the launch will fail.

The default value of this attribute is [CU_DEVICE_ATTRIBUTE_MAX_SHARED_MEMORY_PER_BLOCK](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1ggae12b8a782bebe21b1ac0091bf9f4e2a3a708d91d4570063af37ee8e722d0cf32c) - [CU_FUNC_ATTRIBUTE_SHARED_SIZE_BYTES](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1gga9d955dde0904a9b43ca4d875ac1551bca15651a634781263c9d4ee6070a3991f4), except when [CU_FUNC_ATTRIBUTE_SHARED_SIZE_BYTES](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1gga9d955dde0904a9b43ca4d875ac1551bca15651a634781263c9d4ee6070a3991f4) is greater than [CU_DEVICE_ATTRIBUTE_MAX_SHARED_MEMORY_PER_BLOCK](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1ggae12b8a782bebe21b1ac0091bf9f4e2a3a708d91d4570063af37ee8e722d0cf32c), then the default value of this attribute is 0. The value can be increased to [CU_DEVICE_ATTRIBUTE_MAX_SHARED_MEMORY_PER_BLOCK_OPTIN](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1ggae12b8a782bebe21b1ac0091bf9f4e2a3ae788564c0a95b866dc624fbc1b49dab3) - [CU_FUNC_ATTRIBUTE_SHARED_SIZE_BYTES](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1gga9d955dde0904a9b43ca4d875ac1551bca15651a634781263c9d4ee6070a3991f4).

This attribute is ignored if [CU_FUNC_ATTRIBUTE_SHARED_MEMORY_MODE](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1gga9d955dde0904a9b43ca4d875ac1551bcafc295e3e638dd4ee1e835164f8c55c5d) or [CU_LAUNCH_ATTRIBUTE_SHARED_MEMORY_MODE](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1gga6f6565b334be6bb3134868e10bbdd331a1381331bbd1ffea04cbbad23b6aae988) is set.

This attribute cannot be used to access oversized shared memory. Oversized shared memory can only be accessed by setting [CU_FUNC_ATTRIBUTE_SHARED_MEMORY_MODE](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1gga9d955dde0904a9b43ca4d875ac1551bcafc295e3e638dd4ee1e835164f8c55c5d) or [CU_LAUNCH_ATTRIBUTE_SHARED_MEMORY_MODE](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1gga6f6565b334be6bb3134868e10bbdd331a1381331bbd1ffea04cbbad23b6aae988).

See [cuFuncSetAttribute](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__EXEC.html#group__cuda__exec_1ga0e37dce0173bc883aa1e5b14dd747f26), [cuKernelSetAttribute](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__LIBRARY.html#group__cuda__library_1ga1093ade718915249de3b14320d567067).

CU_FUNC_ATTRIBUTE_MAX_THREADS_PER_BLOCK.doc:
The maximum number of threads per block, beyond which a launch of the function would fail.

This number depends on both the function and the device on which the function is currently loaded.

CU_FUNC_ATTRIBUTE_NON_PORTABLE_CLUSTER_S.doc:
Whether the function can be launched with non-portable cluster size.

1 is allowed, 0 is disallowed. A non-portable cluster size may only function on the specific SKUs the program is tested on. The launch might fail if the program is run on a different hardware platform.

CUDA API provides cudaOccupancyMaxActiveClusters to assist with checking whether the desired size can be launched on the current device.

Portable Cluster Size

A portable cluster size is guaranteed to be functional on all compute capabilities higher than the target compute capability. The portable cluster size for sm_90 is 8 blocks per cluster. This value may increase for future compute capabilities.

The specific hardware unit may support higher cluster sizes that’s not guaranteed to be portable.

See [cuFuncSetAttribute](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__EXEC.html#group__cuda__exec_1ga0e37dce0173bc883aa1e5b14dd747f26), [cuKernelSetAttribute](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__LIBRARY.html#group__cuda__library_1ga1093ade718915249de3b14320d567067).

CU_FUNC_ATTRIBUTE_NUM_REGS.doc: The number of registers used by each thread of this function.

CU_FUNC_ATTRIBUTE_PREFERRED_SHARED_MEMOR.doc:
On devices where the L1 cache and shared memory use the same hardware resources, this sets the shared memory carveout preference, in percent of the total shared memory.

Refer to [CU_DEVICE_ATTRIBUTE_MAX_SHARED_MEMORY_PER_MULTIPROCESSOR](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1ggae12b8a782bebe21b1ac0091bf9f4e2a3a06a33c18889f6fc907412451c95154ed). This is only a hint, and the driver can choose a different ratio if required to execute the function.

See [cuFuncSetAttribute](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__EXEC.html#group__cuda__exec_1ga0e37dce0173bc883aa1e5b14dd747f26), [cuKernelSetAttribute](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__LIBRARY.html#group__cuda__library_1ga1093ade718915249de3b14320d567067).

CU_FUNC_ATTRIBUTE_PTX_VERSION.doc:
The PTX virtual architecture version for which the function was compiled.

This value is the major PTX version \* 10 + the minor PTX version, so a PTX version 1.3 function would return the value 13. Note that this may return the undefined value of 0 for cubins compiled prior to CUDA 3.0.

CU_FUNC_ATTRIBUTE_REQUIRED_CLUSTER_DEPTH.doc:
The required cluster depth in blocks.

The values must either all be 0 or all be positive. The validity of the cluster dimensions is otherwise checked at launch time.

If the value is set during compile time, it cannot be set at runtime. Setting it at runtime should return [`CUresult::CUDA_ERROR_NOT_PERMITTED`].

See [cuFuncSetAttribute](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__EXEC.html#group__cuda__exec_1ga0e37dce0173bc883aa1e5b14dd747f26), [cuKernelSetAttribute](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__LIBRARY.html#group__cuda__library_1ga1093ade718915249de3b14320d567067).

CU_FUNC_ATTRIBUTE_REQUIRED_CLUSTER_HEIGH.doc:
The required cluster height in blocks.

The values must either all be 0 or all be positive. The validity of the cluster dimensions is otherwise checked at launch time.

If the value is set during compile time, it cannot be set at runtime. Setting it at runtime should return [`CUresult::CUDA_ERROR_NOT_PERMITTED`].

See [cuFuncSetAttribute](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__EXEC.html#group__cuda__exec_1ga0e37dce0173bc883aa1e5b14dd747f26), [cuKernelSetAttribute](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__LIBRARY.html#group__cuda__library_1ga1093ade718915249de3b14320d567067).

CU_FUNC_ATTRIBUTE_REQUIRED_CLUSTER_WIDTH.doc:
The required cluster width in blocks.

The values must either all be 0 or all be positive. The validity of the cluster dimensions is otherwise checked at launch time.

If the value is set during compile time, it cannot be set at runtime. Setting it at runtime will return [`CUresult::CUDA_ERROR_NOT_PERMITTED`].

See [cuFuncSetAttribute](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__EXEC.html#group__cuda__exec_1ga0e37dce0173bc883aa1e5b14dd747f26), [cuKernelSetAttribute](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__LIBRARY.html#group__cuda__library_1ga1093ade718915249de3b14320d567067).

CU_FUNC_ATTRIBUTE_SHARED_MEMORY_MODE.doc:
The shared memory mode of a function.

The value type is CUsharedMemoryMode / cudaSharedMemoryMode.

See [cuFuncSetAttribute](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__EXEC.html#group__cuda__exec_1ga0e37dce0173bc883aa1e5b14dd747f26), [cuKernelSetAttribute](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__LIBRARY.html#group__cuda__library_1ga1093ade718915249de3b14320d567067).

CU_FUNC_ATTRIBUTE_SHARED_SIZE_BYTES.doc:
The size in bytes of statically-allocated shared memory required by this function.

This does not include dynamically-allocated shared memory requested by the user at runtime.

CU_FUNC_CACHE_PREFER_EQUAL.doc: prefer equal sized L1 cache and shared memory.

CU_FUNC_CACHE_PREFER_L1.doc: prefer larger L1 cache and smaller shared memory.

CU_FUNC_CACHE_PREFER_NONE.doc: no preference for shared memory or L1 (default).

CU_FUNC_CACHE_PREFER_SHARED.doc: prefer larger shared memory and smaller L1 cache.

CU_GET_PROC_ADDRESS_DEFAULT.doc: Default search mode for driver symbols.

CU_GET_PROC_ADDRESS_LEGACY_STREAM.doc: Search for legacy versions of driver symbols.

CU_GET_PROC_ADDRESS_PER_THREAD_DEFAULT_S.doc: Search for per-thread versions of driver symbols.

CU_GET_PROC_ADDRESS_SYMBOL_NOT_FOUND.doc: Symbol was not found in search.

CU_GET_PROC_ADDRESS_VERSION_NOT_SUFFICIE.doc: Symbol was found but version supplied was not sufficient.

CU_GL_DEVICE_LIST_ALL.doc: The CUDA devices for all GPUs used by the current OpenGL context.

CU_GL_DEVICE_LIST_CURRENT_FRAME.doc: The CUDA devices for the GPUs used by the current OpenGL context in its currently rendering frame.

CU_GL_DEVICE_LIST_NEXT_FRAME.doc: The CUDA devices for the GPUs to be used by the current OpenGL context in the next frame.

CU_GPU_DIRECT_RDMA_WRITES_ORDERING_ALL_D.doc: Any CUDA device in the system can consistently consume remote writes to this device.

CU_GPU_DIRECT_RDMA_WRITES_ORDERING_NONE.doc:
The device does not natively support ordering of remote writes.

[cuFlushGPUDirectRDMAWrites()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__DEVICE.html#group__cuda__device_1ga265e3c82ef0f0fe035f85c4c45a8fbdf) can be leveraged if supported.

CU_GPU_DIRECT_RDMA_WRITES_ORDERING_OWNER.doc: Natively, the device can consistently consume remote writes, although other CUDA devices may not.

CU_GRAPH_CHILD_GRAPH_OWNERSHIP_CLONE.doc:
Default behavior for a child graph node.

Child graph is cloned into the parent and memory allocation/free nodes can’t be present in the child graph.

CU_GRAPH_CHILD_GRAPH_OWNERSHIP_INVALID.doc:
Invalid ownership flag.

Set when params are queried to prevent accidentally reusing the driver-owned graph object.

CU_GRAPH_CHILD_GRAPH_OWNERSHIP_MOVE.doc:
The child graph is moved to the parent.

The handle to the child graph is owned by the parent and will be destroyed when the parent is destroyed.

The following restrictions apply to child graphs after they have been moved: Cannot be independently instantiated or destroyed; Cannot be added as a child graph of a separate parent graph; Cannot be used as an argument to cuGraphExecUpdate; Cannot have additional memory allocation or free nodes added.

CU_GRAPH_COND_TYPE_IF.doc:
Conditional ‘if/else’ Node.

Body[0] executed if condition is non-zero. If `size` == 2, an optional ELSE graph is created and this is executed if the condition is zero.

CU_GRAPH_COND_TYPE_SWITCH.doc:
Conditional ‘switch’ Node.

Body[n] is executed once, where ‘n’ is the value of the condition. If the condition does not match a body index, no body is launched.

CU_GRAPH_COND_TYPE_WHILE.doc:
Conditional ‘while’ Node.

Body executed repeatedly while condition value is non-zero.

CU_GRAPH_DEBUG_DOT_FLAGS_BATCH_MEM_OP_NO.doc: Adds batch mem op node parameters to output.

CU_GRAPH_DEBUG_DOT_FLAGS_CONDITIONAL_NOD.doc: Adds conditional node parameters to output.

CU_GRAPH_DEBUG_DOT_FLAGS_EVENT_NODE_PARA.doc: Adds CUevent handle from record and wait nodes to output.

CU_GRAPH_DEBUG_DOT_FLAGS_HANDLES.doc: Adds node handles and every kernel function handle to output.

CU_GRAPH_DEBUG_DOT_FLAGS_MEM_ALLOC_NODE_.doc: Adds memory alloc node parameters to output.

CU_GRAPH_DEBUG_DOT_FLAGS_MEM_FREE_NODE_P.doc: Adds memory free node parameters to output.

CU_GRAPH_DEBUG_DOT_FLAGS_RUNTIME_TYPES.doc: Use CUDA Runtime structures for output.

CU_GRAPH_DEBUG_DOT_FLAGS_VERBOSE.doc: Output all debug data as if every debug flag is enabled.

CU_GRAPH_DEPENDENCY_TYPE_PROGRAMMATIC.doc:
This dependency type allows the downstream node to use cudaGridDependencySynchronize().

It may only be used between kernel nodes, and must be used with either the [CU_GRAPH_KERNEL_NODE_PORT_PROGRAMMATIC](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1ga888716de0c02411816a952c8426aef75) or [CU_GRAPH_KERNEL_NODE_PORT_LAUNCH_ORDER](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1ga2ed63d6106e76f6966b52c6a0814e789) outgoing port.

CU_GRAPH_EXEC_UPDATE_ERROR.doc: The update failed for an unexpected reason which is described in the return value of the function.

CU_GRAPH_EXEC_UPDATE_ERROR_ATTRIBUTES_CH.doc: The update failed because the node attributes changed in a way that is not supported.

CU_GRAPH_EXEC_UPDATE_ERROR_FUNCTION_CHAN.doc: The update failed because the function of a kernel node changed (CUDA driver < 11.2).

CU_GRAPH_EXEC_UPDATE_ERROR_NODE_TYPE_CHA.doc: The update failed because a node type changed.

CU_GRAPH_EXEC_UPDATE_ERROR_NOT_SUPPORTED.doc: The update failed because something about the node is not supported.

CU_GRAPH_EXEC_UPDATE_ERROR_PARAMETERS_CH.doc: The update failed because the parameters changed in a way that is not supported.

CU_GRAPH_EXEC_UPDATE_ERROR_TOPOLOGY_CHAN.doc: The update failed because the topology changed.

CU_GRAPH_EXEC_UPDATE_ERROR_UNSUPPORTED_F.doc: The update failed because the function of a kernel node changed in an unsupported way.

CU_GRAPH_MEM_ATTR_RESERVED_MEM_CURRENT.doc: (value type = cuuint64_t) Amount of memory, in bytes, currently allocated for use by the CUDA graphs asynchronous allocator.

CU_GRAPH_MEM_ATTR_RESERVED_MEM_HIGH.doc: (value type = cuuint64_t) High watermark of memory, in bytes, currently allocated for use by the CUDA graphs asynchronous allocator.

CU_GRAPH_MEM_ATTR_USED_MEM_CURRENT.doc: (value type = cuuint64_t) Amount of memory, in bytes, currently associated with graphs.

CU_GRAPH_MEM_ATTR_USED_MEM_HIGH.doc:
(value type = cuuint64_t) High watermark of memory, in bytes, associated with graphs since the last time it was reset.

High watermark can only be reset to zero.

CU_GRAPH_NODE_TYPE_BATCH_MEM_OP.doc: Batch MemOp Node See cuStreamBatchMemOp and [CUstreamBatchMemOpType](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1gab257b534afdb704b6ebdb99c16a5b292) for what these nodes can do.

CU_GRAPH_NODE_TYPE_GRAPH.doc: Node which executes an embedded graph.

CU_GRAPH_RECAPTURE_ELIGIBLE_FOR_UPDATE.doc: Node is eligible for update in an instantiated graph.

CU_GRAPH_RECAPTURE_ERROR.doc:
Error while attempting to recapture the node.

The recapture will be ended regardless of the return value from the callback.

CU_GRAPH_RECAPTURE_INELIGIBLE_FOR_UPDATE.doc: Parameter changes in the node cannot be applied to an instantiated graph.

CU_GRAPH_USER_OBJECT_MOVE.doc: Transfer references from the caller rather than creating new references.

CU_GREEN_CTX_DEFAULT_STREAM.doc: Creates a default stream to use inside the green context.

CU_HOST_TASK_BLOCKING.doc: The execution thread will block until new host tasks are ready to run.

CU_HOST_TASK_SPINWAIT.doc: The execution thread will spin wait until new host tasks are ready to run.

CU_IPC_MEM_LAZY_ENABLE_PEER_ACCESS.doc: Automatically enable peer access between remote devices as needed.

CU_JIT_BINARY_LOADER_THREAD_COUNT.doc:
This option specifies the maximum number of concurrent threads to use when compiling device code.

If the specified value is 1, the option will be ignored. If the specified value is 0, the number of threads will match the number of CPUs on the underlying machine. Otherwise, if the option is N, then up to N threads will be used. This option is ignored if the env var CUDA_BINARY_LOADER_THREAD_COUNT is set. Option type: unsigned int

Applies to: compiler and linker.

CU_JIT_CACHE_MODE.doc:
Specifies whether to enable caching explicitly (-dlcm)

Choice is based on supplied ::CUjit_cacheMode_enum.

Option type: unsigned int for enumerated type ::CUjit_cacheMode_enum

Applies to: compiler only.

CU_JIT_ERROR_LOG_BUFFER_SIZE_BYTES.doc:
IN: Log buffer size in bytes.

Log messages will be capped at this size (including null terminator)

OUT: Amount of log buffer filled with messages

Option type: unsigned int

Applies to: compiler and linker.

CU_JIT_FALLBACK_STRATEGY.doc:
Specifies choice of fallback strategy if matching cubin is not found.

Choice is based on supplied [CUjit_fallback](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1ga4a1a92ea65e18b06907b981848c282f2)

. This option cannot be used with cuLink\* APIs as the linker requires exact matches.

Option type: unsigned int for enumerated type.

CU_JIT_FAST_COMPILE.doc: This jit option is used for internal purpose only.

CU_JIT_FMA.doc: Only valid with LTO-IR compiled with toolkits prior to CUDA 12.0.

CU_JIT_FTZ.doc: Only valid with LTO-IR compiled with toolkits prior to CUDA 12.0.

CU_JIT_GENERATE_DEBUG_INFO.doc:
Specifies whether to create debug information in output (-g) (0: false, default)

Option type: int.

CU_JIT_GENERATE_LINE_INFO.doc:
Generate line number information (-lineinfo) (0: false, default)

Option type: int.

CU_JIT_GLOBAL_SYMBOL_ADDRESSES.doc:
Array of host addresses that will be used to relocate corresponding device symbols stored in [CU_JIT_GLOBAL_SYMBOL_NAMES](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1gga5527fa8030d5cabedc781a04dbd1997daa4942ac1cbfb5b2a43994e2acfe3cce0).

Must contain [CU_JIT_GLOBAL_SYMBOL_COUNT](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1gga5527fa8030d5cabedc781a04dbd1997dad6274c174e780689d0eeddd0a9ce1073)

entries.

Option type: void \*\*.

CU_JIT_GLOBAL_SYMBOL_COUNT.doc:
Number of entries in [CU_JIT_GLOBAL_SYMBOL_NAMES](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1gga5527fa8030d5cabedc781a04dbd1997daa4942ac1cbfb5b2a43994e2acfe3cce0) and [CU_JIT_GLOBAL_SYMBOL_ADDRESSES](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1gga5527fa8030d5cabedc781a04dbd1997da9ed137c8a50c7fac811ef7a63c5ae74f) arrays.

Option type: unsigned int

Applies to: dynamic linker only.

CU_JIT_GLOBAL_SYMBOL_NAMES.doc:
Array of device symbol names that will be relocated to the corresponding host addresses stored in [CU_JIT_GLOBAL_SYMBOL_ADDRESSES](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1gga5527fa8030d5cabedc781a04dbd1997da9ed137c8a50c7fac811ef7a63c5ae74f).

Must contain [CU_JIT_GLOBAL_SYMBOL_COUNT](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1gga5527fa8030d5cabedc781a04dbd1997dad6274c174e780689d0eeddd0a9ce1073)

entries.

When loading a device module, driver will relocate all encountered unresolved symbols to the host addresses.

It is only allowed to register symbols that correspond to unresolved global variables.

It is illegal to register the same device symbol at multiple addresses.

Option type: const char \*\*

Applies to: dynamic linker only.

CU_JIT_INFO_LOG_BUFFER_SIZE_BYTES.doc:
IN: Log buffer size in bytes.

Log messages will be capped at this size (including null terminator)

OUT: Amount of log buffer filled with messages

Option type: unsigned int

Applies to: compiler and linker.

CU_JIT_INPUT_CUBIN.doc:
Compiled device-class-specific device code

Applicable options: none.

CU_JIT_INPUT_FATBINARY.doc:
Bundle of multiple cubins and/or PTX of some device code

Applicable options: PTX compiler options,.

CU_JIT_INPUT_LIBRARY.doc:
Archive of host objects with embedded device code

Applicable options: PTX compiler options,.

CU_JIT_INPUT_NVVM.doc: Only valid with LTO-IR compiled with toolkits prior to CUDA 12.0.

CU_JIT_INPUT_OBJECT.doc:
Host object with embedded device code

Applicable options: PTX compiler options,.

CU_JIT_INPUT_PTX.doc:
PTX source code

Applicable options: PTX compiler options.

CU_JIT_LOG_VERBOSE.doc:
Generate verbose log messages (0: false, default)

Option type: int.

CU_JIT_LTO.doc: Only valid with LTO-IR compiled with toolkits prior to CUDA 12.0.

CU_JIT_MAX_REGISTERS.doc:
Max number of registers that a thread may use.

Option type: unsigned int

Applies to: compiler only.

CU_JIT_MAX_THREADS_PER_BLOCK.doc:
Maximum number threads in a thread block, computed as the product of the maximum extent specifed for each dimension of the block.

This limit is guaranteed not to be exeeded in any invocation of the kernel. Exceeding the maximum number of threads results in runtime error or kernel launch failure. For kernels already using PTX directive .maxntid, this option will be ignored by default. Use [CU_JIT_OVERRIDE_DIRECTIVE_VALUES](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1gga5527fa8030d5cabedc781a04dbd1997da504fc22695a386ac14ee66250bbc3a2d)

to let this option take precedence over the PTX directive. Option type: int

Applies to: compiler only.

CU_JIT_MIN_CTA_PER_SM.doc:
This option hints to the JIT compiler the minimum number of CTAs from the kernel’s grid to be mapped to a SM.

This option is ignored when used together with [CU_JIT_MAX_REGISTERS](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1gga5527fa8030d5cabedc781a04dbd1997da09d22b367aad5ca99cca6fe95043896b) or [CU_JIT_THREADS_PER_BLOCK](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1gga5527fa8030d5cabedc781a04dbd1997dae2d4d9ff4fbd21f21039f182616ba1fc). Optimizations based on this option need [CU_JIT_MAX_THREADS_PER_BLOCK](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1gga5527fa8030d5cabedc781a04dbd1997da8685acb8251abf7b9bed80ff58fd29ca) to be specified as well. For kernels already using PTX directive .minnctapersm, this option will be ignored by default. Use [CU_JIT_OVERRIDE_DIRECTIVE_VALUES](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1gga5527fa8030d5cabedc781a04dbd1997da504fc22695a386ac14ee66250bbc3a2d)

to let this option take precedence over the PTX directive. Option type: unsigned int

CU_JIT_OPTIMIZE_UNUSED_DEVICE_VARIABLES.doc: Only valid with LTO-IR compiled with toolkits prior to CUDA 12.0.

CU_JIT_OVERRIDE_DIRECTIVE_VALUES.doc:

Applies to: compiler only.

CU_JIT_SPLIT_COMPILE.doc:
This option specifies the maximum number of concurrent threads to use when running compiler optimizations.

If the specified value is 1, the option will be ignored. If the specified value is 0, the number of threads will match the number of CPUs on the underlying machine. Otherwise, if the option is N, then up to N threads will be used. Option type: unsigned int

Applies to: compiler only.

Target is chosen based on supplied [CUjit_target](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1gae443308cb7ed1d52b85b487305779184).

CU_JIT_THREADS_PER_BLOCK.doc:
IN: Specifies minimum number of threads per block to target compilation for

OUT: Returns the number of threads the compiler actually targeted.

This restricts the resource utilization of the compiler (e.g. max registers) such that a block with the given number of threads should be able to launch based on register limitations. Note, this option does not currently take into account any other resource limitations, such as shared memory utilization.

Cannot be combined with

.

Option type: unsigned int.

Option type: float.

CU_LAUNCH_ATTRIBUTE_DEVICE_UPDATABLE_KER.doc:
Valid for graph nodes, launches.

This attribute is graphs-only, and passing it to a launch in a non-capturing stream will result in an error.

::CUlaunchAttributeValue::deviceUpdatableKernelNode::deviceUpdatable can only be set to 0 or 1. Setting the field to 1 indicates that the corresponding kernel node should be device-updatable. On success, a handle will be returned via ::CUlaunchAttributeValue::deviceUpdatableKernelNode::devNode which can be passed to the various device-side update functions to update the node’s kernel parameters from within another kernel. For more information on the types of device updates that can be made, as well as the relevant limitations thereof, see ::cudaGraphKernelNodeUpdatesApply.

. Graphs containing one or more device-updatable nodes also do not allow multiple instantiation, and neither the graph nor its instantiated version can be passed to cuGraphExecUpdate.

If a graph contains device-updatable nodes and updates those nodes from the device from within the graph, the graph must be uploaded with.

CU_LAUNCH_ATTRIBUTE_LAUNCH_COMPLETION_EV.doc:

to record the event.

Nominally, the event is triggered once all blocks of the kernel have begun execution. Currently this is a best effort. If a kernel B has a launch completion dependency on a kernel A, B may wait until A is complete. Alternatively, blocks of B may begin before all blocks of A have begun, for example if B can claim execution resources unavailable to A (e.g. they run on different GPUs) or if B is a higher priority than A. Exercise caution if such an ordering inversion could lead to deadlock.

set except that it is not visible to cudaGridDependencySynchronize() and can be used with compute capability less than 9.0.

CU_LAUNCH_ATTRIBUTE_MEM_SYNC_DOMAIN.doc:

CU_LAUNCH_ATTRIBUTE_NVLINK_UTIL_CENTRIC_.doc:
Valid for streams, graph nodes, launches.

This attribute is a hint to the CUDA runtime that the launch should attempt to make the kernel maximize its NVLINK utilization.

When possible to honor this hint, CUDA will assume each block in the grid launch will carry out an even amount of NVLINK traffic, and make a best-effort attempt to adjust the kernel launch based on that assumption.

This attribute is a hint only. CUDA makes no functional or performance guarantee. Its applicability can be affected by many different factors, including driver version (i.e. CUDA doesn’t guarantee the performance characteristics will be maintained between driver versions or a driver update could alter or regress previously observed perf characteristics.) It also doesn’t guarantee a successful result, i.e. applying the attribute may not improve the performance of either the targeted kernel or the encapsulating application.

Valid values for CUlaunchAttributeValue::nvlinkUtilCentricScheduling are 0 (disabled) and 1 (enabled).

CU_LAUNCH_ATTRIBUTE_PORTABLE_CLUSTER_SIZ.doc:
Valid for graph nodes, launches.

This controls whether the kernel launch is allowed to use a non-portable cluster size. Valid values for [CUlaunchAttributeValue::portableClusterSizeMode](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/unionCUlaunchAttributeValue.html#unionculaunchattributevalue_1ab59ceb6906a7de4ce07de5f2269d18b3) are described in [CUlaunchAttributePortableClusterMode](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1gaeb6323dd92d20fdf48e4cf68122e77a1). Any other value will return [CUDA_ERROR_INVALID_VALUE](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1ggac6c391505e117393cc2558fff6bfc2e9a90696c86fcee1f536a1ec7d25867feeb).

CU_LAUNCH_ATTRIBUTE_PREFERRED_CLUSTER_DI.doc:
Valid for graph nodes, launches.

Set [CUlaunchAttributeValue::preferredClusterDim](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/unionCUlaunchAttributeValue.html#unionculaunchattributevalue_1ad78976fd10fa7429385d312a34df8c5a) to allow the kernel launch to specify a preferred substitute cluster dimension. Blocks may be grouped according to either the dimensions specified with this attribute (grouped into a “preferred substitute cluster”), or the one specified with [CU_LAUNCH_ATTRIBUTE_CLUSTER_DIMENSION](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1gga6f6565b334be6bb3134868e10bbdd331af1a227eb6283f2a292cf5a38cdceb638)

attribute (grouped into a “regular cluster”). The cluster dimensions of a “preferred substitute cluster” shall be an integer multiple greater than zero of the regular cluster dimensions. The device will attempt - on a best-effort basis - to group thread blocks into preferred clusters over grouping them into regular clusters. When it deems necessary (primarily when the device temporarily runs out of physical resources to launch the larger preferred clusters), the device may switch to launch the regular clusters instead to attempt to utilize as much of the physical device resources as possible.

Each type of cluster will have its enumeration / coordinate setup as if the grid consists solely of its type of cluster. For example, if the preferred substitute cluster dimensions double the regular cluster dimensions, there might be simultaneously a regular cluster indexed at (1,0,0), and a preferred cluster indexed at (1,0,0). In this example, the preferred substitute cluster (1,0,0) replaces regular clusters (2,0,0) and (3,0,0) and groups their blocks.

CU_LAUNCH_ATTRIBUTE_PREFERRED_SHARED_MEM.doc:
Valid for launches.

On devices where the L1 cache and shared memory use the same hardware resources, setting [CUlaunchAttributeValue::sharedMemCarveout](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/unionCUlaunchAttributeValue.html#unionculaunchattributevalue_1ab4890866538ded7d27e648d399caaff2) to a percentage between 0-100 signals the CUDA driver to set the shared memory carveout preference, in percent of the total shared memory for that kernel launch. This attribute takes precedence over [CU_FUNC_ATTRIBUTE_PREFERRED_SHARED_MEMORY_CARVEOUT](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1gga9d955dde0904a9b43ca4d875ac1551bcac75f6fd470b848653f026b8c82c10ae3). This is only a hint, and the CUDA driver can choose a different configuration if required for the launch.

CU_LAUNCH_ATTRIBUTE_PRIORITY.doc:
Valid for streams, graph nodes, launches.

See [CUlaunchAttributeValue::priority](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/unionCUlaunchAttributeValue.html#unionculaunchattributevalue_1a8b3a370124a50866fcdb1c9cb5580e96).

CU_LAUNCH_ATTRIBUTE_PROGRAMMATIC_EVENT.doc:
Valid for launches.

Set [CUlaunchAttributeValue::programmaticEvent](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/unionCUlaunchAttributeValue.html#unionculaunchattributevalue_1ae1eb628b29c538c9fb1e5a3d829b0777) to record the event. Event recorded through this launch attribute is guaranteed to only trigger after all block in the associated kernel trigger the event. A block can trigger the event through PTX launchdep.release or CUDA builtin function cudaTriggerProgrammaticLaunchCompletion(). A trigger can also be inserted at the beginning of each block’s execution if triggerAtBlockStart is set to non-0. The dependent launches can choose to wait on the dependency using the programmatic sync (cudaGridDependencySynchronize() or equivalent PTX instructions). Note that dependents (including the CPU thread calling [cuEventSynchronize()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__EVENT.html#group__cuda__event_1ga9e520d34e51af7f5375610bca4add99c)) are not guaranteed to observe the release precisely when it is released. For example, [cuEventSynchronize()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__EVENT.html#group__cuda__event_1ga9e520d34e51af7f5375610bca4add99c)

may only observe the event trigger long after the associated kernel has completed. This recording type is primarily meant for establishing programmatic dependency between device tasks. Note also this type of dependency allows, but does not guarantee, concurrent execution of tasks.

The event supplied must not be an interprocess or interop event. The event must disable timing (i.e. must be created with the.

CU_LAUNCH_ATTRIBUTE_PROGRAMMATIC_STREAM_.doc:
Valid for launches.

Setting [CUlaunchAttributeValue::programmaticStreamSerializationAllowed](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/unionCUlaunchAttributeValue.html#unionculaunchattributevalue_1a21590ca9c3de21690d12d9c7f73917ab) to non-0 signals that the kernel will use programmatic means to resolve its stream dependency, so that the CUDA runtime should opportunistically allow the grid’s execution to overlap with the previous kernel in the stream, if that kernel requests the overlap. The dependent launches can choose to wait on the dependency using the programmatic sync (cudaGridDependencySynchronize() or equivalent PTX instructions).

This controls a kernel’s use of non-portable or oversized shared memory configurations.

CU_LIBRARY_BINARY_IS_PRESERVED.doc:
Specifes that the argument `code` passed to [cuLibraryLoadData()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__LIBRARY.html#group__cuda__library_1ga957f12ff5af4166f43c89d17cfb0a74d) will be preserved.

Specifying this option will let the driver know that `code` can be accessed at any point until [cuLibraryUnload()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__LIBRARY.html#group__cuda__library_1ga24969cb24138171edf465bc8669d5914). The default behavior is for the driver to allocate and maintain its own copy of `code`. Note that this is only a memory usage optimization hint and the driver can choose to ignore it if required. Specifying this option with [cuLibraryLoadFromFile()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__LIBRARY.html#group__cuda__library_1ga88cff489fab37c7fd1985ceb61023205) is invalid and will return [CUDA_ERROR_INVALID_VALUE](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1ggac6c391505e117393cc2558fff6bfc2e9a90696c86fcee1f536a1ec7d25867feeb).

CU_LIMIT_CIG_ENABLED.doc:
A non-zero value indicates this CUDA context is a CIG-enabled context.

Can only be queried, cannot be set.

CU_LIMIT_CIG_SHMEM_FALLBACK_ENABLED.doc: When set to zero, CUDA will fail to launch a kernel on a CIG context, instead of using the fallback path, if the kernel uses more shared memory than available.

CU_LIMIT_DEV_RUNTIME_PENDING_LAUNCH_COUN.doc: GPU device runtime pending launch count.

CU_LIMIT_DEV_RUNTIME_SYNC_DEPTH.doc: GPU device runtime launch synchronize depth.

This is a hint.

CU_LIMIT_PERSISTING_L2_CACHE_SIZE.doc: A size in bytes for L2 persisting lines cache size.

CU_LIMIT_SHMEM_SIZE.doc:
A maximum size in bytes of shared memory available to CUDA kernels on a CIG context.

Can only be queried, cannot be set.

CU_LOGICAL_ENDPOINT_FLAG_COUNTED_OPS.doc: Indicate the programmer’s intention to use counted operations with the logical endpoint.

CU_LOGICAL_ENDPOINT_FLAG_NONE.doc: Default flag for logical endpoint construction.

CU_MEMCPY_FLAG_PREFER_OVERLAP_WITH_COMPU.doc: Hint to the driver to try and overlap the copy with compute work on the SMs.

CU_MEMCPY_OPERAND_TYPE_POINTER.doc: Memcpy operand is a valid pointer.

CU_MEMCPY_SRC_ACCESS_ORDER_ANY.doc:
Indicates that access to the source pointer can be out of stream order and the accesses can happen even after the API call returns.

This flag is suited for host pointers allocated outside CUDA (ex., via malloc) when it’s known that no prior operations in the stream can be accessing the memory. Specifying this flag allows the driver to optimize the copy on certain platforms.

CU_MEMCPY_SRC_ACCESS_ORDER_DURING_API_CA.doc:
Indicates that access to the source pointer can be out of stream order and all accesses must be complete before the API call returns.

This flag is suited for ephemeral sources (ex., stack variables) when it’s known that no prior operations in the stream can be accessing the memory and also that the lifetime of the memory is limited to the scope that the source variable was declared in. Specifying this flag allows the driver to optimize the copy and removes the need for the user to synchronize the stream after the API call.

CU_MEMCPY_SRC_ACCESS_ORDER_STREAM.doc: Indicates that access to the source pointer must be in stream order.

CU_MEMPOOL_ATTR_ALLOCATION_TYPE.doc: (value type = CUmemAllocationType) The allocation type of the mempool.

CU_MEMPOOL_ATTR_EXPORT_HANDLE_TYPES.doc:
(value type = CUmemAllocationHandleType) Available export handle types for the mempool.

For imported pools this value is always [`CUmemAllocationHandleType::CU_MEM_HANDLE_TYPE_NONE`] as an imported pool cannot be re-exported.

CU_MEMPOOL_ATTR_HW_DECOMPRESS_ENABLED.doc: (value type = int) Indicates whether the pool has hardware compresssion enabled.

CU_MEMPOOL_ATTR_LOCALITY_DOMAIN_ID.doc:
(value type = int) The locality domain ID for the mempool, if the mempool is localized to a locality domain.

A value of -1 indicates that the mempool is not localized.

Note: On devices with a single locality domain, mempools created with [CU_MEM_LOCATION_TYPE_DEVICE_LOCALITY_DOMAIN](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1gga75cfd5b9fa5c1c6ee2be2547bfbe882ea178b51df01f1de90894a00ce1c131f25) and localityDomainId 0 are equivalent to full-device mempools created with [CU_MEM_LOCATION_TYPE_DEVICE](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1gga75cfd5b9fa5c1c6ee2be2547bfbe882eaa4409aa6b414995d628a320eafbbbb6e). The value of this attribute will be -1 for such mempools.

CU_MEMPOOL_ATTR_LOCATION_ID.doc:
(value type = int) The location id for the mempool.

If the location type for this pool is [`CUmemLocationType::CU_MEM_LOCATION_TYPE_INVISIBLE`] then ID will be CU_DEVICE_INVALID.

CU_MEMPOOL_ATTR_LOCATION_TYPE.doc:
(value type = CUmemLocationType) The location type for the mempool.

For imported memory pools where the device is not directly visible to the importing process or pools imported via fabric handles across nodes this will be [`CUmemLocationType::CU_MEM_LOCATION_TYPE_INVISIBLE`].

CU_MEMPOOL_ATTR_MAX_POOL_SIZE.doc:
(value type = cuuint64_t) Maximum size of the pool in bytes, this value may be higher than what was initially passed to cuMemPoolCreate due to alignment requirements.

A value of 0 indicates no maximum size. For [`CUmemAllocationType::CU_MEM_ALLOCATION_TYPE_MANAGED`] and IPC imported pools this value will be system dependent.

CU_MEMPOOL_ATTR_RELEASE_THRESHOLD.doc:
(value type = cuuint64_t) Amount of reserved memory in bytes to hold onto before trying to release memory back to the OS.

When more than the release threshold bytes of memory are held by the memory pool, the allocator will try to release memory back to the OS on the next call to stream, event or context synchronize. (default 0).

CU_MEMPOOL_ATTR_RESERVED_MEM_CURRENT.doc: (value type = cuuint64_t) Amount of backing memory currently allocated for the mempool.

CU_MEMPOOL_ATTR_RESERVED_MEM_HIGH.doc:
(value type = cuuint64_t) High watermark of backing memory allocated for the mempool since the last time it was reset.

High watermark can only be reset to zero.

CU_MEMPOOL_ATTR_REUSE_ALLOW_INTERNAL_DEP.doc: (value type = int) Allow cuMemAllocAsync to insert new stream dependencies in order to establish the stream ordering required to reuse a piece of memory released by cuMemFreeAsync (default enabled).

CU_MEMPOOL_ATTR_REUSE_ALLOW_OPPORTUNISTI.doc:
(value type = int) Allow reuse of already completed frees when there is no dependency between the free and allocation.

(default enabled).

CU_MEMPOOL_ATTR_REUSE_FOLLOW_EVENT_DEPEN.doc:
(value type = int) Allow cuMemAllocAsync to use memory asynchronously freed in another streams as long as a stream ordering dependency of the allocating stream on the free action exists.

CUDA events and null stream interactions can create the required stream ordered dependencies. (default enabled).

CU_MEMPOOL_ATTR_USED_MEM_CURRENT.doc: (value type = cuuint64_t) Amount of memory from the pool that is currently in use by the application.

CU_MEMPOOL_ATTR_USED_MEM_HIGH.doc:
(value type = cuuint64_t) High watermark of the amount of memory from the pool that was in use by the application since the last time it was reset.

High watermark can only be reset to zero.

CU_MEM_ACCESS_FLAGS_PROT_NONE.doc: Default, make the address range not accessible.

CU_MEM_ACCESS_FLAGS_PROT_READ.doc: Make the address range read accessible.

CU_MEM_ACCESS_FLAGS_PROT_READWRITE.doc: Make the address range read-write accessible.

CU_MEM_ADVISE_SET_ACCESSED_BY.doc: Data will be accessed by the specified device, so prevent page faults as much as possible.

CU_MEM_ADVISE_SET_PREFERRED_LOCATION.doc: Set the preferred location for the data as the specified device.

CU_MEM_ADVISE_SET_READ_MOSTLY.doc: Data will mostly be read and only occasionally be written to.

CU_MEM_ALLOC_GRANULARITY_RECOMMENDED.doc: Recommended granularity for allocation for best performance.

CU_MEM_ATTACH_GLOBAL.doc: Memory can be accessed by any stream on any device.

CU_MEM_ATTACH_HOST.doc: Memory cannot be accessed by any stream on any device.

CU_MEM_ATTACH_SINGLE.doc: Memory can only be accessed by a single stream on the associated device.

CU_MEM_LOCATION_TYPE_DEVICE.doc: Location is a device location, thus id is a device ordinal.

CU_MEM_LOCATION_TYPE_DEVICE_LOCALITY_DOM.doc: Location is a portion of device memory, specified by the locality domain ID.

CU_MEM_LOCATION_TYPE_HOST.doc: Location is host, id is ignored.

CU_MEM_LOCATION_TYPE_HOST_NUMA.doc: Location is a host NUMA node, thus id is a host NUMA node id.

CU_MEM_LOCATION_TYPE_HOST_NUMA_CURRENT.doc: Location is a host NUMA node of the current thread, id is ignored.

CU_MEM_LOCATION_TYPE_INVISIBLE.doc: Location is not visible but device is accessible, id is always CU_DEVICE_INVALID.

CU_MEM_LOCATION_TYPE_NONE.doc:

CU_MEM_RANGE_ATTRIBUTE_ACCESSED_BY.doc: Memory range has [CU_MEM_ADVISE_SET_ACCESSED_BY](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1ggacfe2ed2d4567745dd4ad41034136fff3aa44e5c0ad0a77d05332739848e181a2d) set for specified device.

CU_MEM_RANGE_ATTRIBUTE_LAST_PREFETCH_LOC.doc: The last location to which the range was prefetched.

CU_MEM_RANGE_ATTRIBUTE_PREFERRED_LOCATIO.doc: The preferred location of the range.
The preferred location id of the range.
The preferred location type of the range.

CU_MEM_RANGE_ATTRIBUTE_READ_MOSTLY.doc: Whether the range will mostly be read and only occasionally be written to.

CU_MEM_RANGE_FLAG_DMA_BUF_MAPPING_TYPE_P.doc: Indicates that DMA_BUF handle should be mapped via PCIe BAR1.

CU_OCCUPANCY_DISABLE_CACHING_OVERRIDE.doc: Assume global caching is enabled and cannot be automatically turned off.

CU_POINTER_ATTRIBUTE_ACCESS_FLAGS.doc: Returns the access flags the device associated with the current context has on the corresponding memory referenced by the pointer given.

CU_POINTER_ATTRIBUTE_ACCESS_FLAG_NONE.doc: No access, meaning the device cannot access this memory at all, thus must be staged through accessible memory in order to complete certain operations.

CU_POINTER_ATTRIBUTE_ACCESS_FLAG_READ.doc: Read-only access, meaning writes to this memory are considered invalid accesses and thus return error in that case.

CU_POINTER_ATTRIBUTE_ACCESS_FLAG_READWRI.doc: Read-write access, the device has full read-write access to the memory.

CU_POINTER_ATTRIBUTE_ALLOWED_HANDLE_TYPE.doc: Bitmask of allowed [CUmemAllocationHandleType](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1ga450a23153d86fce0afe30e25d63caef9) for this allocation.

CU_POINTER_ATTRIBUTE_BUFFER_ID.doc: A process-wide unique ID for an allocated memory region.

CU_POINTER_ATTRIBUTE_CONTEXT.doc: The [CUcontext](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1gaf9f5bd81658f866613785b3a0bb7d7d9) on which a pointer was allocated or registered.

CU_POINTER_ATTRIBUTE_DEVICE_ORDINAL.doc: A device ordinal of a device on which a pointer was allocated or registered.

CU_POINTER_ATTRIBUTE_DEVICE_POINTER.doc: The address at which a pointer’s memory may be accessed on the device.

CU_POINTER_ATTRIBUTE_HOST_POINTER.doc: The address at which a pointer’s memory may be accessed on the host.

CU_POINTER_ATTRIBUTE_IS_GPU_DIRECT_RDMA_.doc: 1 if the memory this pointer is referencing can be used with the GPUDirect RDMA API.

CU_POINTER_ATTRIBUTE_IS_HW_DECOMPRESS_CA.doc: Returns in `*data` a boolean that indicates whether the pointer points to memory that is capable to be used for hardware accelerated decompression.

CU_POINTER_ATTRIBUTE_IS_LEGACY_CUDA_IPC_.doc: 1 if this pointer maps to an allocation that is suitable for ::cudaIpcGetMemHandle, 0 otherwise.

CU_POINTER_ATTRIBUTE_IS_MANAGED.doc: Indicates if the pointer points to managed memory.

CU_POINTER_ATTRIBUTE_LOCALITY_DOMAIN_ORD.doc: Returns in `*data` an integer representing the locality domain ordinal of the memory allocation, or -1 if the allocation is not localized to a locality domain.

CU_POINTER_ATTRIBUTE_MAPPED.doc: 1 if this pointer is in a valid address range that is mapped to a backing allocation, 0 otherwise.

CU_POINTER_ATTRIBUTE_MAPPING_BASE_ADDR.doc: The start address of the mapping that the pointer belongs to.

CU_POINTER_ATTRIBUTE_MAPPING_SIZE.doc: Size of the actual underlying mapping that the pointer belongs to.

CU_POINTER_ATTRIBUTE_MEMORY_BLOCK_ID.doc: A process-wide unique id corresponding to the physical allocation the pointer belongs to.

CU_POINTER_ATTRIBUTE_MEMORY_TYPE.doc: The [CUmemorytype](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1ga8a114cc994ad2e865c44ef3838eaec72) describing the physical location of a pointer.

CU_POINTER_ATTRIBUTE_MEMPOOL_HANDLE.doc:
Returns the mempool handle for the allocation if it was allocated from a mempool.

Otherwise returns NULL.

CU_POINTER_ATTRIBUTE_P2P_TOKENS.doc: A pair of tokens for use with the nv-p2p.h Linux kernel interface.

CU_POINTER_ATTRIBUTE_RANGE_SIZE.doc: Size of the address range for this requested pointer.

CU_POINTER_ATTRIBUTE_RANGE_START_ADDR.doc: Starting address for this requested pointer.

CU_POINTER_ATTRIBUTE_SYNC_MEMOPS.doc: Synchronize every synchronous memory operation initiated on this region.

CU_PREFER_BINARY.doc: Prefer to fall back to compatible binary code if exact match not found.

CU_PREFER_PTX.doc: Prefer to compile ptx if exact binary match not found.

CU_PROCESS_STATE_CHECKPOINTED.doc: Application memory contents have been checkpointed and underlying allocations and device handles have been released.

CU_PROCESS_STATE_CHECKPOINTING.doc: Application memory contents are being checkpointed.

CU_PROCESS_STATE_FAILED.doc: Application entered an uncorrectable error during the checkpoint/restore process.

CU_PROCESS_STATE_RESTORING.doc: Application memory contents are being restored.

CU_RES_VIEW_FORMAT_NONE.doc: No resource view format (use underlying resource format).

CU_SHAREDMEM_CARVEOUT_DEFAULT.doc: No preference for shared memory or L1 (default).

CU_SHAREDMEM_CARVEOUT_MAX_L1.doc: Prefer maximum available L1 cache, minimum shared memory.

CU_SHAREDMEM_CARVEOUT_MAX_SHARED.doc: Prefer maximum available shared memory, minimum L1 cache.

CU_SHARED_MEMORY_MODE_ALLOW_NON_PORTABLE.doc: Specifies that the dynamic shared size bytes requested may be a non-portable size but still within the bounds of [CU_DEVICE_ATTRIBUTE_MAX_SHARED_MEMORY_PER_BLOCK_OPTIN](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1ggae12b8a782bebe21b1ac0091bf9f4e2a3ae788564c0a95b866dc624fbc1b49dab3).

CU_SHARED_MEMORY_MODE_ALLOW_OVERSIZED_SH.doc: Specifies that oversized shared memory configurations may be used (with the limitation of only 8kB L1 cache).

CU_SHARED_MEMORY_MODE_DEFAULT.doc: The default to use for shared memory on launch - uses current function attribute for [CU_FUNC_ATTRIBUTE_MAX_DYNAMIC_SHARED_SIZE_BYTES](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1gga9d955dde0904a9b43ca4d875ac1551bca75b33d145e83462ef7292575015be03e).

CU_SHARED_MEMORY_MODE_PREFER_OVERSIZED_S.doc: Specifies that oversized shared memory configurations may be used (with the limitation of only 8kB L1 cache), and prefer an oversized shared memory configuration.

CU_SHARED_MEMORY_MODE_REQUIRE_PORTABLE.doc: Specifies that the dynamic shared size bytes requested must be a portable size within the bounds of [CU_DEVICE_ATTRIBUTE_MAX_SHARED_MEMORY_PER_BLOCK](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1ggae12b8a782bebe21b1ac0091bf9f4e2a3a708d91d4570063af37ee8e722d0cf32c).

CU_SHARED_MEM_CONFIG_DEFAULT_BANK_SIZE.doc: set default shared memory bank size.

CU_SHARED_MEM_CONFIG_EIGHT_BYTE_BANK_SIZ.doc: set shared memory bank width to eight bytes.

CU_SHARED_MEM_CONFIG_FOUR_BYTE_BANK_SIZE.doc: set shared memory bank width to four bytes.

CU_STREAM_CAPTURE_STATUS_INVALIDATED.doc: Stream is part of a capture sequence that has been invalidated, but not terminated.

CU_STREAM_MEMORY_BARRIER_TYPE_GPU.doc: Limit memory barrier scope to the GPU.

CU_STREAM_MEM_OP_BARRIER.doc: Insert a memory barrier of the specified type.

CU_STREAM_MEM_OP_FLUSH_REMOTE_WRITES.doc: This has the same effect as [CU_STREAM_WAIT_VALUE_FLUSH](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1ggaf16864e8693d888f8178067470001b21a5dd93e7173619c943fae495568f4d771), but as a standalone operation.

CU_STREAM_NON_BLOCKING.doc: Stream does not synchronize with stream 0 (the NULL stream).

CU_STREAM_SET_CAPTURE_DEPENDENCIES.doc: Replace the dependency set with the new nodes.

CU_STREAM_WAIT_VALUE_FLUSH.doc:
Follow the wait operation with a flush of outstanding remote writes.

This means that, if a remote write operation is guaranteed to have reached the device before the wait can be satisfied, that write is guaranteed to be visible to downstream device work. The device is permitted to reorder remote writes internally. For example, this flag would be required if two remote writes arrive in a defined order, the wait is satisfied by the second write, and downstream work needs to observe the first write. Support for this operation is restricted to selected platforms and can be queried with [CU_DEVICE_ATTRIBUTE_CAN_FLUSH_REMOTE_WRITES](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1ggae12b8a782bebe21b1ac0091bf9f4e2a3a4c702e528f71bf513ee0f3f32878ce9d).

CU_STREAM_WAIT_VALUE_GEQ.doc:
Wait until (int32_t)(\*addr - value) >= 0 (or int64_t for 64 bit values).

Note this is a cyclic comparison which ignores wraparound. (Default behavior.)

CU_STREAM_WAIT_VALUE_NOR.doc:
Wait until ~(\*addr | value) != 0.

Support for this operation can be queried with [cuDeviceGetAttribute()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__DEVICE.html#group__cuda__device_1ga9c3e1414f0ad901d3278a4d6645fc266) and [CU_DEVICE_ATTRIBUTE_CAN_USE_STREAM_WAIT_VALUE_NOR](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__cuda__types_1ggae12b8a782bebe21b1ac0091bf9f4e2a3abe06f9c31c264e0b29be6cc6330b5047).

CU_STREAM_WRITE_VALUE_NO_MEMORY_BARRIER.doc:
Permits the write to be reordered with writes which were issued before it, as a performance optimization.

Normally, cuStreamWriteValue32 will provide a memory fence before the write, which has similar semantics to __threadfence_system() but is scoped to the stream rather than a CUDA thread. This flag is not supported in the v2 API.
